Also used where individual short breaks are recorded using legal status V1); L = change of legal status (where the underlying reason a child is looked after changes but placement does not change); P = change of placement only (where legal status does not change); B = change of both legal status and placement status on the same day.

Table Description: Episodes of care. Data items which relate to individual episodes of care, which either start or end during the census period
Column Description: An integer indicating the number of short term breaks (legal status V1) the child received. Short breaks are provided to children and young people with care and support needs, to provide them with opportunities to engage in activities outside the home, or to give their parents (or guardians) some “respite” from the normal duties of looking after the child, or both. They can be a one-off event, but often they are usually planned breaks, often in the same setting or with the same provider. Under the terms of the 2014 Act and the 2015 Regulations, they are only actually being looked after for those days (and nights) when they are being accommodated and are not looked after when they are back home with their parents (or guardians).

Table Description: Looked after children anonymised identifiers
Column Description: Anonymised Linking Field (ALF). This is the encrypted person identifier for linking across SAIL Databank datasets. The NHS number is not used to assign an ALF in the CIN census data. Instead the Unique Pupil Number (UPN) is used to access the child's name and address to match a child to an ALF using a trusted third party (Digital Health and Care Wales). A UPN is automatically allocated to each child in maintained nursery or primary schools, therefore children may have a UPN from age of 2 or 3 onwards.

Table Description: Looked after children anonymised identifiers
Column Description: Anonymised Linked Field Match Percentage. This number is a match % score from probabalistic matching, when joining together anonymised data. This linkage process consists of matching against the Welsh Demographic Service by NHS number, where a valid number exists, and where there is no valid number then matching is attempted using first name, surname, date of birth, and postcode. This is an artificial score with no real-world meaning; i.e. a match of .99 does not mean there is a 99% chance the match is correct. This number is assigned when deriving the Encrypted Anonymised Linking Field.
